description: How should domain state be persisted and retrieved?
question: What is your default approach for persisting domain state?

options.name: Repository Abstraction
options.description: Repository pattern abstracts persistence. Domain objects are persistence-ignorant. Repository handles save/load.
options.when_to_use: Clean domain model, testability priority, multiple storage backends possible, DDD approach
options.example: OrderRepository: Saves order, Finds by id, Finds by customer. Order has no persistence knowledge

options.name: Active Record
options.description: Domain objects know how to persist themselves. Save/load methods on the object itself.
options.when_to_use: Simple CRUD, rapid development, object-relational mapping, framework support (Rails, Django)
options.example: Order: Saves to database, Loads by id, Deletes. Order contains persistence logic

options.name: Event Sourcing
options.description: State stored as sequence of events. Current state derived by replaying events. Full audit trail.
options.when_to_use: Audit requirements, temporal queries, complex domain logic, event-driven architecture
options.example: Order stored as: OrderCreated, LineItemAdded, LineItemAdded, PaymentReceived, OrderShipped events

options.name: Unit of Work
options.description: Track changes to objects during business transaction. Commit all changes atomically at end.
options.when_to_use: Complex transactions, multiple aggregates, optimistic concurrency, ORM integration
options.example: UnitOfWork tracks: modified Order, new LineItems, deleted Discounts. Commits all at once

options.name: CQRS Separation
options.description: Separate models for commands (writes) and queries (reads). Optimized for each use case.
options.when_to_use: Complex queries, read/write ratio skewed, different scaling needs, eventual consistency OK
options.example: OrderCommandModel for placing orders. OrderQueryModel (denormalized) for order history views
